name: CORS reflects arbitrary Origin / allow-all origin function
attack_scenario: attacker.example serves a page that fetch()es https://victim.app/account with credentials; the server reflects Origin: attacker.example, the browser exposes the response, and the attacker reads the victim's private account data.
negative_test_hint: send a credentialed request with Origin "https://attacker.example" and assert the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header does not echo it

exemplar.explanation: Echoing the request's Origin header inline into Access-Control-Allow-Origin (or an AllowOriginFunc that unconditionally returns true) makes every website a trusted origin. Combined with Allow-Credentials this lets any attacker page read authenticated responses. The safe form hoists the header into a variable and reflects it only after an allowlist check, which does not match. Set Vary: Origin as well.
